implementation_approach: Implement order cancellation by extending the Order model with cancellation state fields (status enum or cancelledAt timestamp), adding validation logic to the mock API client to enforce business rules (time window checks, status verification), creating a new cancellation endpoint following existing API patterns, enhancing the OrderHistoryPage component with conditional cancel buttons and confirmation modal, updating the error handling to include cancellation-specific error codes, and modifying the orderStorage layer to persist cancellation state. The implementation leverages existing architectural patterns: feature-sliced architecture for file organization, established API wrapper patterns in orderApi.ts, existing error handling infrastructure via ApiError class, and React hooks for component state management. Cancellation validation enforces time-window constraints (orders can only be cancelled within 24-48 hours of creation), checks current order status, and verifies user ownership.
coupling_observations: The implementation introduces moderate coupling patterns: (1) Order model extension cascades through multiple layers - any model field addition affects API responses, storage serialization, and component rendering; (2) Mock client.ts becomes the integration point for business logic validation - centralizes rules but increases file size; (3) OrderHistoryPage tightly couples data loading, error handling, and cancellation logic within same component - future refactoring may extract sub-components; (4) Cancellation status must coordinate with existing reviewStatus field to prevent invalid state combinations; (5) Error handling integrates with existing ApiError infrastructure - minimal new coupling; (6) Storage layer backward compatibility maintained through optional fields; (7) No external system coupling - purely internal feature. The layered architecture contains coupling well, but the monolithic mock client and component complexity are primary concerns.
duplication_observations: Duplication is well-controlled due to existing abstractions: (1) Error handling pattern already established - cancellation errors map naturally to errorMessages.ts codes; (2) API wrapper pattern established in orderApi.ts - cancelOrder function mirrors existing createOrder and getMyOrders structure; (3) Async state management pattern exists in OrderHistoryPage - loading and error states already handled by useState/try-catch; (4) Button component infrastructure supports disabled state - no need for new button variants; (5) Confirmation dialog/modal is first of its kind - should be extracted to shared/ui/Modal for future reuse (delete confirmation, batch operations); (6) Storage persistence pattern mirrors existing saveOrder and replaceOrderHistory - no significant duplication; (7) Validation rule duplication risk if business logic not centralized - mock client is correct home for all validation. Only significant opportunity is extracting confirmation modal to reusable component.
responsibility_observations: Proper separation of concerns requires: (1) Order entity model (entities/order/model.ts) defines structure only - OrderStatus type, cancelledAt, cancellationReason, cancellableUntil fields without embedded logic; (2) API wrapper (orderApi.ts) provides thin client facade - cancelOrder(orderId) function abstracts backend endpoint; (3) Mock API client (shared/api/client.ts) owns all business validation logic - time window checks, status verification, user ownership validation; (4) OrderHistoryPage orchestrates UI - displays buttons conditionally, shows confirmation modal, handles user interactions, delegates validation to API; (5) errorMessages.ts purely translates error codes - no logic; (6) orderStorage.ts handles persistence only - saveOrder, replaceOrderHistory, getMyOrders; (7) Modal/Button components are pure presentation. This architecture prevents responsibility creep and enables future refactoring.
changeability_observations: The feature establishes patterns for future order state transitions: (1) Order model gains cancellationReason field - extensible for audit trails, analytics, retention policies; (2) Time-window calculation in mock client supports future customization - store-specific policies, order-type-specific windows, promotional extensions; (3) Error codes are extensible - new cancellation errors don't affect existing error handling; (4) Modal extraction enables reuse - delete order, return request, reschedule - future features benefit; (5) Status-based conditional rendering in OrderHistoryPage scales to other actions - reschedule, modify, appeal; (6) Mock cancellation endpoint is migration-ready - no client-side changes when moving to real backend; (7) Storage layer supports status evolution - if lifecycle grows to state machine, backward compatible; (8) Future complexity: as order states grow (pending→confirmed→ready→completed/cancelled/returned/refunded), consider state machine pattern. Current implementation avoids this premature complexity but supports clean migration. Cancellation reason optional field enables future 'required reason' feature without breaking changes.
